title: Gemilut Chasadim: Kindness for Anyone
hookLine: a daily act of chesed, however small
carry: chesed goes to rich and poor alike
tomorrow: a rabbi is known by two words from a Psalm. which two, and why?

lines: A MERGE, AN ELEVATOR, A COFFEE.
THE WORLD STANDS ON THREE THINGS.
THE THIRD FITS IN A HALLWAY.
cards: Someone lets you merge on a packed road. A stranger holds the elevator. A coworker remembers how you take your coffee.

None of it makes the news, and the day is lighter anyway. In Pirkei Avot, Simon the Righteous says the world stands on three things: on Torah, on the service of God, and on acts of loving-kindness. So which fits in a day?
The third needs no book and no building. It fits in a hallway.

teach.b: The Hebrew is gemilut chasadim, doing kindnesses, from chesed. It's the word under Micah's line, "to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God": the mercy there is chesed.
And the Talmud makes a surprising claim.
Acts of kindness, it says, are greater than tzedakah in three ways. Tzedakah is done with money; kindness, with your body or your money. Tzedakah goes to the poor; kindness, to the poor and the rich.

Tzedakah is for the living; kindness, for the living and the dead, like caring for a burial. So the pushke can't do this job for you, and nobody is too comfortable to need it. Now a neighbor who says it too.

teach.h: ISLAM: EVERY GOOD DEED IS CHARITY.
teach.b: In Islam, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari to have said: every good deed is charity. In that saying, any good deed, not only money, counts as sadaqah, giving.
The same instinct: the smallest kindness is on the books. And one honest difference.
That saying stretches one word, charity, to cover every good deed. The Talmud keeps two words, tzedakah and chesed, and sets them side by side, each with its own job. Two maps of the same ground.
Something to tell a friend tonight: the Talmud says kindness can be done even for the rich.

how: Jewish communities organize gemilut chasadim through visiting the sick, free loan societies, meals for new parents and mourners, and burial societies; individuals often make a daily small kindness part of a personal practice.

games.q: what does “one kindness a day” mean?
o: one small act of care, done for anyone, daily
a weekly gift of money to people in need
being polite to strangers whenever you can

games.q: kindness, two traditions — tap the pairs.
p: the world stands on three things
to do justly, and to love mercy
body or money, rich or poor

s: kindness is basically the same as giving money to charity
the Talmud separates them: kindness can use your body, and goes to rich and poor, living and dead.
a saying of the Prophet Muhammad calls every good deed charity
Sahih al-Bukhari 6021: any good deed counts as sadaqah, giving.
Judaism and Islam say the same thing about kindness, in the same words
both put small kindness on the books; they draw the map differently: one word, or two.

games.q: your neighbor is wealthy and lives alone since his wife died. he doesn't need anything money can buy. would bringing him dinner be gemilut chasadim?
o: no; kindness, like tzedakah, is for people in need.
yes; the Talmud says kindness goes to the rich and the poor.
only if the dinner cost you real money.
games.why: tzedakah is for the poor; kindness is for the poor and the rich, done with your body as well as your money. dinner counts.

practice: Open your messages and choose one person who'd be glad to hear from you, someone who didn't ask. Write something small and specific: a thank-you, a memory, an offer to help with one real thing.
Send it, and let that be today's kindness, done before the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: One kindness a day: gemilut chasadim, an act of chesed done with your hands, your time or your money, for anyone, rich or poor.

orig.note: Hebrew: loving-kindness, steady loyal love; the 'mercy' in Micah 6:8.

carryVoice: For today: chesed goes to rich and poor alike. Small enough for a hallway, and nobody has to earn it.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 1:2 (Simon the Righteous: the world stands on Torah, service and acts of loving-kindness)

sources.q: to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God

Sahih al-Bukhari 6021 (every good deed is charity)
